banter: Del riffles a stack of chips one-handed. "Sit down, stranger. I'm owed a winning streak and you'll do fine."
"Out there they fold when they're scared. In here we raise. It's more honest."
She grins over her cards. "No markers, Doc says. Pity. My credit's the only thing I've got left."
description: A drifter with a gambler's easy grin and a derringer-shaped bulge at her hip, Del washed into the Reach on somebody else's plane and never left the felt. She plays loose, bluffs like she means it, and tilts when she's losing — which is exactly why the regulars keep her a chair warm. She'll take your money laughing and stand you a drink with it after.

clothing_layers: a dust-red frock coat gone pale at the shoulders
a laced bodice-vest over a loose linen shirt
riding trousers, a plain bra and briefs

name: Delphine "Del" Roan
